chapter: Early life and New Orleans arrival
title: Parents, sisters and music at home
summary: He names his parents, describes his father's fiddle, family quadrilles, coon songs and vaudeville shows at Ramona.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: I don't think we got your father's name, your mother's, and these sisters.

My father's name was Robert Carew. He ran a shoe store there, a small shoe store there in the neighborhood where we lived in Grand Rapids. My mother's name was Rose, now, I'm getting twisted now, Carolyn, Carolyn, Carolyn Rose, uh, Rosely, Carolyn Rosely Johnson. Her name, her maiden name was. Her first name was Carolyn. And, uh, I had four sisters. And, uh, three of them played the piano a little bit. Two of them quite a bit, one just a little, and the third, the fourth, the fourth sister didn't play at all. But we always had plenty of music. My father played the violin and, uh, as a, like a country dance player. He played all the dance music like that. We used to have quadrilles
there at home. You looked at music as a, from a utilitarian standpoint. You looked at it to enjoy it.

It was our, it was our amusement at home, largely. We, we always had plenty of fun at home. We, we went to the extent of, uh, of getting a canvas covering for the parlor carpet, putting it on so we could have quadrilles there and dance on this canvas covered to the front room carpet. And my father would play the fiddle and we would have quadrilles there. And, uh, they were always playing. And, of course, when, when coon songs came along, ragtime coon songs, why, we were strong for them. We got them all that we could pick up all that got popular we tried to get. And, uh, so we had plenty of music all the time at home. And this one sister became a very good player. And she, she also played popular music. We, none of, none of them ever got, got, uh, too high tone to play good popular music. Did you have any mechanical music at home? No, we had no mechanical music at home at all. It was a long time before I ever had any phonograph in the house, even after I got to New Orleans. And, and still you were so interested in music that you'd pick up these coon songs in the ranks. Oh, yes. As they'd come out, we'd get them. If we went to a show and we heard a new song, we'd get that. And that was the way they were spread then, you know. I had a good summer resort near there in Grand Rapids called Ramona. And they, they booked vaudeville from Detroit and the east there. Had some of the best artists there and singers, dancers, coon shouters, minstrel shows came to town. And we were, we were very strong on that. Always went to the shows when we could. Bought the music if we liked it. If anything new came out in that line,
we got it. Well, you were pretty well acquainted with music before you went to New York then.
